title: Kummer-root invariance of regular divisor purity
statement:
For a prime $\ell$ and $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, use ordinary small-etale derived categories and Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. If $W$ is a regular Noetherian scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-regular-scheme], say that $W$ is punctually pure at $w\in W$ when, for $W_w=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{W,w}$, $d_w=\dim\mathcal O_{W,w}$ and its closed-point inclusion $j_w:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)\hookrightarrow W_w$, the Kummer fundamental-class map
$$A_{\kappa(w)}\longrightarrow j_w^!A_{W_w}(d_w)[2d_w]$$
of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] is an isomorphism. Say that $W$ is punctually pure when this holds at every point. Local rings and residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field], affine spectra as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be regular Noetherian with $\ell$ invertible, and let $f\in B$ be a nonzerodivisor with $D=\operatorname{Spec}(B/(f))$ regular. Put
$$X'=\operatorname{Spec}B[U]/(U^\ell-f),\qquad D'=V(U)\subset X'.$$
Write $i:D\hookrightarrow X$ and $i':D'\hookrightarrow X'$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and use polynomial rings as in [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Then $X'$ is regular, $D'\simeq D$ is a regular effective Cartier divisor, and
$$A_D\to i^!A_X(1)[2]\text{ is an isomorphism}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A_{D'}\to i'^!A_{X'}(1)[2]\text{ is an isomorphism}.$$
Empty divisors are allowed. The projection $p:X'\to X$ is finite locally free of rank $\ell$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free], is surjective, and restricts to a surjective etale morphism $X'\setminus D'\to X\setminus D$ [def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.4.5 and its proof, printed pp.246--248 (the monic root algebra, and its Kummer cover away from the divisor).

proof.text: Put $C=B[u]/(u^\ell-f)$. The monic power basis $1,u,\ldots,u^{\ell-1}$ [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] makes $C$ finite free of rank $\ell$; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-algebra-spectrum] gives finite local freeness of $p$, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] makes $C$ Noetherian. Injectivity of multiplication by $f$ on $B$ implies it on the free $B$-module $C$ coefficient by coefficient. Since $u^\ell=f$, $uc=0$ implies $fc=0$, hence $c=0$. Evaluation $u=0$ identifies $C/(u)$ with $B/(f)$, with inverse induced by constants. Thus $D'\simeq D$ is a regular effective Cartier divisor. Each prime of $B$ lifts: in an algebraic closure of its residue field choose a root of the positive-degree polynomial $T^\ell-\bar f$; the kernel of the resulting $C$-map is a prime over the chosen prime. The same argument for primes not containing $f$ gives a root with $u\ne0$, hence surjectivity on the complements. These arguments include the empty spectrum and unit $f$.

At primes of $C$ containing $u$, [lem-sbc-root-algebra-regular-at-root] applies with $R=B$, $n=\ell$: $f$ is a nonzerodivisor and $B/(f)$ is regular. Off $u=0$, $f=u^\ell$ is invertible and [lem-sbc-root-split-away-cover-etale] gives etaleness over $X$. For regularity there apply [lem-sbc-etale-regular-divisor-base-change] to the affine etale map $B\to C[1/f]$ with its auxiliary element $g=1$: multiplication by $1$ is injective and $B/(1)=0$ is regular (it has no primes). Thus $C[1/f]$ is regular. The two loci cover $\operatorname{Spec}C$, proving regularity of $X'$. Together with Step 1 this proves every geometric assertion about $p,D'$.

Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ of $D$, and write $S=\operatorname{Spec}R=X_{(\bar x)}$. The regular local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ has regular strict henselization by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-regular]; its quotient by $f$ is regular by [lem-sbc-strict-hensel-regular-divisor-quotient]. Strict henselization is faithfully flat [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat], so the defining preservation of injections [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] applied to multiplication by $f$ shows that $f$ remains a nonzerodivisor; it lies in the maximal ideal because $x\in D$. Finite base change of strict localizations [lem-trf-finite-base-strict-localization] identifies $X'\times_X S$ with $X'_{(\bar x')}$: its geometric closed fibre has coordinate ring $\Omega[u]/(u^\ell)$, so has precisely one connected component and one geometric point $\bar x'$. Denote this strict local regular root pair by $(S_1,D_1)$. It has equation $u^\ell=f$ and $D_1\simeq D\times_X S$. Thus the complements $U=S\setminus D_S$ and $U_1=S_1\setminus D_1$ are exactly the two complements needed by the strict-local divisor criterion for the corresponding points.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.5, reduction at a geometric point of D, printed p.246

proof.text: Use [lem-per-kummer-classifying-purity-criterion] for $(R,f)$. Choose a topological generator of $G=\mathbf Z_\ell(1)$. Under $G\simeq\mathbf Z_\ell$, [lem-exc-procyclic-two-term] with coefficient ring $A=\mathbf F_\ell$ and $s=1$ gives $H^q(BG,A)=0$ for $q\ge2$. The new tower lemma supplies isomorphisms in degrees $0,1$ for $a_A:R\Gamma(BG,A)\to R\Gamma(U,A)$. Since derived sections of a degree-zero sheaf have no negative cohomology, $a_A$ is an isomorphism exactly when $H^q(U,A)=0$ for all $q\ge2$. The same argument applies to $(S_1,D_1)$ with parameter $u$, since Step 3 supplies its strictly local regular hypotheses. These are tests for the divisor pair, not for the closed point as a higher-codimension immersion.

The tower lemma also supplies the cartesian square with $g:U_1\to U$ and $g':BG\to BG$ induced by multiplication by $\ell$. Apply [lem-per-kummer-relative-cone-functor] with $H=\ell G$, identified with $G$ by multiplication by $\ell$. It produces the $A$-linear triangulated relative functor $F$, and the finite permutation module $M=g'_*A=\operatorname{Map}(G/\ell G,A)$. The map $a_A$ is an isomorphism iff $F(A)=0$. The second finite-cover comparison identifies $a_M$ with $R\Gamma(BG,A)\to R\Gamma(U_1,A)$ for the shifted tower; it is an isomorphism iff $F(M)=0$. These identifications use the direct image $g'_*$, not inverse image: $M$ has rank $\ell$, whereas $g'^*A=A$.

source.place: Paragraphs between Lemmas 3.4.8 and 3.4.9, printed pp.247–248

proof.text: Write $Q=G/\ell G$, choose its cyclic generator $\sigma$, and set $z=\sigma-1$. The permutation module $M=\operatorname{Map}(Q,A)$ has the cyclic delta-function basis; identify it $G$-equivariantly with $A[Q]=A[z]/(z^\ell)$ by $\sigma^i\mapsto\delta_{\sigma^i}$. If the convention gives inverse translation instead, use $\delta_{\sigma^{-i}}$. The relation is $(\sigma-1)^\ell=\sigma^\ell-1=0$ in characteristic $\ell$, and $1,z,\ldots,z^{\ell-1}$ is another basis by the triangular change from $1,\sigma,\ldots,\sigma^{\ell-1}$. Put $M_i=A[z]/(z^i)$ for $1\le i\le\ell$, and $M_0=0$. For $i\ge1$, multiplication by $z^{i-1}$ identifies the trivial module $A$ with the kernel of the quotient $M_i\to M_{i-1}$. This gives explicit exact sequences $0\to A\to M_i\to M_{i-1}\to0$. They are exact already on the displayed bases, are $G$-equivariant, and $M_\ell=M$.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.5 final paragraph, explicit cyclic augmentation filtration, printed p.248

proof.text:
The short exact sequences in Step 6 give distinguished triangles $A	o M_i	o M_{i-1}	o A[1]$ in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of discrete $A[G]$-modules by [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle]; their terms are concentrated in degree $0$, so they lie in $D^+$. The functor $F$ is triangulated by [lem-per-kummer-relative-cone-functor], so their images have long exact cohomology sequences by [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact]. If $F(A)=0$, induction starting with $M_0=0$ gives $F(M_i)=0$ for every $i$. Conversely, if $F(A)
e0$, bounded-below cohomology gives a least $n$ with $H^nF(A)
e0$. Induction on $i$, using the same long exact sequences, shows $H^kF(M_i)=0$ for $k<n$. The segment $H^{n-1}F(M_{i-1})	o H^nF(A)	o H^nF(M_i)$ then has zero first term, so its second map is injective for every $i\ge1$. In particular $H^nF(M_\ell)
e0$. Thus $F(A)=0$ iff $F(M)=0$. Together with Steps 4–5 this proves $H^q(U,A)=0$ for all $q\ge2$ iff the same holds for $U_1$.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.5 final paragraph, first nonzero cohomology argument, printed p.248

proof.text: Finally apply [lem-per-divisor-purity-strict-local-criterion] to the original pair $(X,D)$ and the regular pair $(X',D')$. Its hypotheses hold by Steps 1–2. The isomorphism $D'\simeq D$ identifies their geometric points, and Step 3 identifies the strict local complements with $U,U_1$ for every such point. Step 7 equates the required vanishing tests at each point. Hence the two global supported Kummer class maps are isomorphisms simultaneously. If $D$ is empty there are no geometric points to test and both maps are maps of zero sheaves on the empty scheme, so the same conclusion holds.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.5, pointwise equivalence and conclusion, printed pp.246–248
